assertion_analysis.fails_if: an explicit f=1 or cross-field argument changes any solution field or the iron field, because both are compared bit-exactly against the omitted-fill solve.

the gain term, both component orders of N, the per-cell fill or the iron_magnetisation division is wrong; the expected value comes from an independent elimination of the internal iron field, not from the solver.
a zero or >1 fill, a (0,) or 2-component fill, a negative or >1 factor, or a non-finite value is accepted, because _galerkin_interaction is poisoned to prove the refusal precedes assembly.
the gain operand is dropped from the residual OR the residual stops being the stated constitutive law; the same point scores 0 with the gain and >0.1 of the reference norm without it.
either receipt error passes its 10%/11% bound, proven by raising the stored row to limit+1e-6 and requiring the refusal; it also fails if the receipt's device or 0.4 factor stops being asserted.
the one-third smear ratio check is removed or loosened, proven by doubling the smear error to a 0.5 ratio and requiring the refusal.
the section factor stops improving on the plain fill by at least half on the 0.10 m grid; it cannot fail on the absolute bound, which was deliberately moved to the 0.032 m receipt.
the tolerance is reverted to a zero absolute allowance (rejecting 1e-16-of-scale noise) or loosened past a 1e-9 relative change of a dominant element.

evidence_caveats: The fine-grid acceptance is asserted from the external receipt /work/projects/imas_gpu/sophelio/evidence/iron-limb-fill/production/material-refinement-20261114/summary.json, not recomputed by a test; I re-read that receipt and the 0.032 m rows reproduce 5.244561% and 10.659474% with device NVIDIA H200 NVL.

The dispatch's evidence fence says at most ten Newton corrections while plan section 2 and its own parenthetical (twelve at 0.04 m) say fifteen; the measured 6 and 12 meet the plan, and the earlier ten-correction budget stop is disclosed in the fragment.

The 0.08 m and 0.032 m measurements predate the head revision; git log over nova/biot/magnetisation.py shows the production module unchanged from 2c87ab9f to 5b63d8e7, which is what makes those rows applicable.
I re-ran tests/test_magnetisation.py::test_explicit_unit_fill_preserves_solid_solution at the reviewed head as a doubt check: 2 passed in 56.52s.

0.reason: The 1e-12 baseline capture is a multi-megabyte receipt and nova keeps such receipts out of git; the unit-fill test in tests/test_magnetisation.py guards the default path in the repository and the full capture comparison (68 captures, zero mismatches) is recorded in the landed evidence.

findings.text: non-blocking: the node's 1e-12 omission-invariance check runs only when NOVA_MATERIAL_BASELINE names a captured npz, and that baseline (baseline-outputs.npz) lives in the run directory rather than the repository, so a clone cannot re-check the plan's first done-when clause and only the new unit-fill test guards the default path.

non-blocking: validate_control_receipt asserts the geometry bounds, the one-third smear reduction and the presence of the fitted and plain rows, but never the plan's solid-outline f=1 control that must exceed 100% on the same measure, so a regression that made the solid arm resemble the filled solve would redden no gate.

item_verdicts.diff: I read all 28 commits from bf61ef594ce36cb3fb75cbf57fc592e1185ffd4f to 5b63d8e79ced75662e165a0a40154e09f5be2bc5 (no merges) and the +1517/-4 diff adds two solver keywords, a seven-operand residual branch, two solution fields, 17 test cases and the scripts/iron_limb_production measurement, gate, compatibility and negative-control harness.
item_verdicts.done_when: The quantitative clause is the 10%/11% fine-grid bound plus the one-third smear reduction; scripts/iron_limb_production/gate.py:44 sets both bounds, tests/test_magnetisation.py:1157 and :1181 call the validator, and the recorded head arm log states COMPATIBILITY mismatches=0 and 70 passed, though the plan's solid-outline f=1 control is recorded only in the evidence table and asserted by no gate.
item_verdicts.goal: The dispatched goal is a per-cell toroidal fill fraction and cross-field factor in the production axisymmetric iron solve; nova/biot/magnetisation.py:542-543 adds both as scalar, (cells,) or centroid-callback arguments and nova/biot/magnetisation.py:421-431 applies them in the residual, with the iron's own magnetisation and permeability exposed at nova/biot/magnetisation.py:482 and :650.
item_verdicts.manifest: I read manifest.md and its status is complete with the gate command, baseline 53 passed, head 70 passed, the receipt paths and its retry failures; the two arm logs on disk end with those same summary lines and EXIT=0, so the claim reconciles.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The dispatch declares nova/biot/magnetisation.py, tests/test_magnetisation.py, scripts/iron_limb_production and docs/evidence/fragments/iron-limb-fill-fraction; git diff --stat bf61ef594ce36cb3fb75cbf57fc592e1185ffd4f..5b63d8e79ced75662e165a0a40154e09f5be2bc5 lists ten files and every one of them lies inside those entries.

justifications.durability: tests/test_magnetisation.py:1040 and :1054 fail if the unit-fill path diverges or the gain term is dropped, but the plan's 1e-12 omission invariance rides on scripts/iron_limb_production/compatibility.py:64, whose baseline capture is not committed.
justifications.evidence: scripts/iron_limb_production/gate.py:44 asserts the recorded receipts/baseline-suite.log and receipts/compatibility-head-suite.log values I re-read (geometry 0.052446/0.106595 against 0.10/0.11, smear ratios 0.122614/0.213281), but the solid-outline control and the midplane/arm ratio table rest on the evidence fragment alone.
justifications.fit: the new helper at nova/biot/magnetisation.py:515 follows the validation idiom of nova/biot/magnetisation.py:515-530 and its sibling _points, and no added name uses a forbidden suffix.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/biot/magnetisation.py:596 appends the fill and gain operands exactly when the fill differs from one, so the per-cell factor reaches the Newton residual at nova/biot/magnetisation.py:421-431 and both new fields are returned at nova/biot/magnetisation.py:657-663.
justifications.reuse: the fill and demagnetising-factor derivations stay in scripts/prototypes/iron_limb_fill/axisymmetric.py and a search of nova/ for a callable-or-scalar field resolver found only the new nova/biot/magnetisation.py:515, so no owner is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff --stat of bf61ef5..5b63d8e lies inside the declared entries, the only edit outside the new keyword path in nova/biot/magnetisation.py being the docstring and dataclass fields it implies.
